input.new_string:
- **🔴 CRITICAL SECURITY — any authed user can self-join any family (full cross-tenant breach).** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit, verified against source.)_ The `family_members` INSERT policy `"Users can insert their own membership"` (`supabase/migrations/20251010000319_remote_schema.sql:324-329`) has `WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid())` — it checks only that you insert **your own** user_id, never that the `family_id` is yours or that an invite exists; `status` defaults to `'active'`. Combined with the world-readable `family_members` SELECT (`USING(true)`, lets you enumerate every `family_id`), any logged-in user can `INSERT (family_id=<victim>, user_id=self)` and become an active member of any family — then every family-scoped policy (receipts, transactions, categories, storage objects, etc.) grants full read/write to that tenant's financial data + receipt images. One request, whole-app tenant breach. **Distinct from the R2–R5 chain above** (which is about the RPCs and reading memberships; this is the self-service *write* into an arbitrary family). Fix: gate membership INSERT behind a verified invite (e.g. an `accept_invite` SECURITY DEFINER RPC), default self-inserts to `'invited'`, and drop the open self-insert policy. Should land with the R2–R5 migration pass. **Highest priority.**
- **🟠 HIGH SECURITY — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint** (`002_profiles_table.sql`). The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix (abuse is by a legit authed user). Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
- **🟡 MEDIUM SECURITY — two more SECURITY DEFINER functions are PUBLIC/anon-executable.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit, verified.)_ `create_default_hierarchy(uuid)` and `create_default_categories(...)` (`20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql`, `20260111000001_migrate_categories_to_family_scope.sql`) are `SECURITY DEFINER` with `GRANT EXECUTE … TO authenticated` but **no `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC`**, so `anon` retains the default grant. `create_default_hierarchy`'s guard is `IF auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS(...membership...)` — for `anon`, `auth.uid()` is NULL so the guard is **skipped** and it seeds hierarchy rows into any family that has none. Bounded to inserting fixed seed rows into empty tenants (integrity/pollution, not disclosure), but it's an unauthenticated write. `search_path` IS correctly pinned on both. Fix: `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM PUBLIC, anon` on both; change the guard to fail-closed (`IF auth.uid() IS NULL OR NOT EXISTS(...) THEN RETURN`). Audit all other `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for the same missing REVOKE while here.
- **🟢 LOW SECURITY / deferred audit items still open (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Still present, unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` unauthenticated + SSRF via caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, incl. svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`) — the secret-prefix leak was fixed in the refactor but these two survived; **M2** `/admin/resize-images` is a client-only page that deletes+re-uploads receipt originals with no authz beyond `confirm()`; **M3** `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding / no limit). Also **F6:** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject (`20260705_email_send_failures.sql`) — confirm intended. Note **`receipts` UPDATE `WITH CHECK`** carries the same `fm.family_id = fm.family_id` tautology as INSERT — already in scope of the PRD's **R3** (which lists both `:347` INSERT and `:370` UPDATE).
- **Remove the abandoned Spending Bridge (waterfall) view. ✅ DONE.**

Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball (`xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/...` via `overrides`) — clears the CVEs, keeps `.xls` support, but adds a non-npm-registry dep that our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — actively maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`** (xlsx/csv only), so it would drop `.xls` support unless paired with a dedicated BIFF parser (`js-xls`). Decision needed on whether legacy `.xls` is still required. Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers the practical risk.

- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie` rather than force it. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix` (non-breaking). Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.

Yes — quite a few, and one is a **new Critical** that arguably outranks the documented chain. I verified the two most serious against source myself; all are now logged in the backlog's Engineering section.

## 🔴 NEW — Critical (verified by me)
**Any authenticated user can self-join any family → full cross-tenant breach.** The `family_members` INSERT policy (`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql:324-329`) is `WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid())` — it only checks you're inserting *your own* user_id, never that the `family_id` is yours or that an invite exists, and `status` defaults to `'active'`. With the world-readable `USING(true)` SELECT to enumerate family_ids, one `INSERT` makes you an active member of any family, and every family-scoped policy then hands you that tenant's receipts, transactions, and images. This is **distinct from the R2–R5 chain** (that's about the RPCs + *reading* memberships; this is a self-service *write* into an arbitrary family). No anon key even needed — any logged-in user. I'd rank this the top priority; it should land in the same migration pass as R2–R5.

## 🟠 NEW — High
**Unverified, non-unique profile emails → email-ingestion hijack.** Profile add-email (`profile/+page.svelte`) attaches any address with no ownership proof and no cross-user uniqueness; the Resend webhook attributes receipts via `find_user_by_email`, which trusts those columns. An attacker can claim a victim's forwarding address and siphon their forwarded receipts, or poison attribution. Not closed by the signature fix (it's a legit authed user).

## 🟡 NEW — Medium (verified by me)
**Two more PUBLIC/anon-executable SECURITY DEFINER functions.** `create_default_hierarchy` and `create_default_categories` have `GRANT … TO authenticated` but **no `REVOKE FROM PUBLIC`**, and `create_default_hierarchy`'s guard (`auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND …`) is *skipped* for anon → unauthenticated seed-writes into empty tenants. Bounded impact (fixed rows), but worth a REVOKE + fail-closed guard, plus a sweep of all other SD functions.

## 🟢 Re-verified: the PRD's 5 deferred items are all still present
- **H3** OCR endpoints still unauthenticated + SSRF (`fileUrl` forwarded to Mistral, no auth, no host allow-list)
- **M1** *partially* fixed — the secret-prefix log was removed in the refactor, but the handler **still logs full request headers** (`handler.ts:334`) and an **API-key prefix/suffix** (`:389`)
- **M2** `/admin/resize-images` still destructive with no authz beyond `confirm()`
- **M3** `families` INSERT still unbounded
- **M4** `xlsx@0.18.5` still the vulnerable npm build (`npm audit`: 1 high, 6 low today)
- Plus **F6 (Low):** `email_send_failures` is whole-family-readable — co-members see each other's notification recipient/subject.

## Areas the sweep found clean
No `{@html}`/XSS, signed-URL expiry and storage write-path (`auth.uid()`-pinned) are sound, file-upload validation uses magic-number sniffing, no service-role/secret leaked to client, and the other tables' RLS (transactions, categories, vendor rules, importance/groups) use correct membership binding — no tautology.

**One correction to the earlier picture:** the receipts *UPDATE* tautology the sweep flagged as "new" is actually already covered by the PRD's **R3** (it lists both `:347` INSERT and `:370` UPDATE) — so no double-counting there.

Everything above is now in `docs/product-backlog.md` (still uncommitted, per your rule). Net: the security surface is materially bigger than the one PRD — I'd treat **F1 (self-join) as co-critical with the R2–R5 chain** and fix them in one migration pass. Want me to draft that consolidated migration set (R2–R5 + F1 + F3) for your review?

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.insert_receipt_with_context(receipt_data jsonb)
 RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
AS $function$
DECLARE
  inserted_receipt jsonb;
  user_id_val uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Extract user_id from the receipt_data
  user_id_val := (receipt_data->>'user_id')::uuid;

  -- Set the local auth.uid() for this transaction
  -- This allows triggers that depend on auth.uid() to work
  PERFORM set_config('request.jwt.claims', json_build_object('sub', user_id_val)::text, true);

  -- Insert the receipt
  INSERT INTO receipts (
    user_id,
    receipt_image_path,
    merchant_name,
    total_amount,
    tax,
    transaction_date,
    currency,
    credit_card_name,

    (receipt_data->>'transaction_date')::date,
    receipt_data->>'currency',
    receipt_data->>'credit_card_name',
    receipt_data->>'credit_card_last_4'
  )
  RETURNING to_jsonb(receipts.*) INTO inserted_receipt;

  RETURN inserted_receipt;
END;

-- Security remediation: collapse the unauthenticated data-forgery chain and the
-- related cross-tenant escalations found in the 2026-07-05 and 2026-07-17 audits.
--
-- Covers Security Remediation PRD R2–R5 plus audit findings F1 and F3. R1 (webhook
-- signature enforcement) already shipped in supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts.
--
-- Runs as a single transaction (all-or-nothing). After applying, run the PRD's
-- "Verification (end-to-end)" checks with a throwaway anon-key script — do NOT add
-- committed e2e tests. None of the changes touch storage.objects (which the
-- migration role does not own), so they are safe to run via `supabase db push`.
--
-- Verified before writing: the only caller of insert_receipt_with_context and
-- find_user_by_email is the service-role Resend webhook; create_default_hierarchy is
-- called by an authenticated client (CategoryService); no production code inserts
-- into family_members (default membership is created by the SECURITY DEFINER
-- ensure_default_family(), which bypasses RLS).

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- R2 — Lock down insert_receipt_with_context (fixes C2 + C2b)
--   Pin search_path, add an auth.users existence guard, and restrict EXECUTE to
--   the service role (the webhook's only legitimate caller).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.insert_receipt_with_context(receipt_data jsonb)
 RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path = public
AS $function$
DECLARE
  inserted_receipt jsonb;
  user_id_val uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Extract user_id from the receipt_data
  user_id_val := (receipt_data->>'user_id')::uuid;

  -- Fail closed on a missing or unknown user_id: the caller must not be able to
  -- spoof an arbitrary/nonexistent subject into request.jwt.claims.
  IF user_id_val IS NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'insert_receipt_with_context: user_id is required';
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM auth.users WHERE id = user_id_val) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'insert_receipt_with_context: unknown user_id %', user_id_val;
  END IF;

  -- Set the local auth.uid() for this transaction so triggers that depend on
  -- auth.uid() (e.g. set_receipt_family_id) work.
  PERFORM set_config('request.jwt.claims', json_build_object('sub', user_id_val)::text, true);

  -- NOTE: this insert deliberately mirrors the pre-existing column set. The
  -- separately-tracked "RPC drops suspicious_date / exchange_rate_to_cad" bug is
  -- out of scope for this security migration and is not changed here.
  INSERT INTO receipts (
    user_id,
    receipt_image_path,
    merchant_name,
    total_amount,
    tax,
    transaction_date,
    currency,
    credit_card_name,
    credit_card_last_4
  )
  VALUES (
    user_id_val,
    receipt_data->>'receipt_image_path',
    receipt_data->>'merchant_name',
    (receipt_data->>'total_amount')::numeric,
    (receipt_data->>'tax')::numeric,
    (receipt_data->>'transaction_date')::date,
    receipt_data->>'currency',
    receipt_data->>'credit_card_name',
    receipt_data->>'credit_card_last_4'
  )
  RETURNING to_jsonb(receipts.*) INTO inserted_receipt;

  RETURN inserted_receipt;
END;
$function$;

REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.insert_receipt_with_context(jsonb) FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.insert_receipt_with_context(jsonb) TO service_role;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- R3 — Fix the tautological receipts write checks (fixes C3)
--   The INSERT and UPDATE WITH CHECK clauses used `fm.family_id = fm.family_id`
--   (always true) instead of `fm.family_id = receipts.family_id`, letting any
--   active member of any family write receipts into an arbitrary family_id.
--   The USING clauses / SELECT / DELETE policies were already correct.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated can insert receipts" ON public.receipts;
CREATE POLICY "Authenticated can insert receipts"
ON public.receipts
AS PERMISSIVE
FOR INSERT
TO public
WITH CHECK (
  ((SELECT auth.uid()) IS NOT NULL)
  AND (
    (family_id IS NULL)
    OR EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM family_members fm
      WHERE fm.family_id = receipts.family_id
        AND fm.user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
        AND fm.status = 'active'
    )
  )
);

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Members can update family receipts" ON public.receipts;
CREATE POLICY "Members can update family receipts"
ON public.receipts
AS PERMISSIVE
FOR UPDATE
TO public
USING (
  ((family_id IS NOT NULL) AND EXISTS (
     SELECT 1 FROM family_members fm
     WHERE fm.family_id = receipts.family_id
       AND fm.user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
       AND fm.status = 'active'))
  OR ((family_id IS NULL) AND ((SELECT auth.uid()) = user_id))
)
WITH CHECK (
  ((family_id IS NOT NULL) AND EXISTS (
     SELECT 1 FROM family_members fm
     WHERE fm.family_id = receipts.family_id
       AND fm.user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
       AND fm.status = 'active'))
  OR ((family_id IS NULL) AND ((SELECT auth.uid()) = user_id))
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- R4 — Restrict find_user_by_email to the service role (fixes H1)
--   Already SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path; only the grant is wrong
--   (defaults to PUBLIC). The webhook (service role) is the only caller.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.find_user_by_email(text) FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.find_user_by_email(text) TO service_role;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- R5 — Scope family_members reads without RLS recursion (fixes H2)
--   Replace the world-readable USING(true) SELECT policy with a membership-scoped
--   one. A SECURITY DEFINER helper reads family_members as owner, breaking the
--   recursion that USING(true) was papering over.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.is_member_of(target_family uuid)
 RETURNS boolean
 LANGUAGE sql
 STABLE
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path = public
AS $function$
  SELECT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.family_members fm
    WHERE fm.family_id = target_family
      AND fm.user_id = auth.uid()
      AND fm.status = 'active'
  );
$function$;

REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.is_member_of(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.is_member_of(uuid) TO authenticated;

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated users can view family memberships" ON public.family_members;
CREATE POLICY "Members can view family memberships"
ON public.family_members
AS PERMISSIVE
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (
  user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
  OR public.is_member_of(family_id)
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- F1 — Remove the open family_members self-insert policy (fixes cross-tenant join)
--   The policy's WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid()) never verified the family_id,
--   so any authed user could INSERT (family_id = <victim>, user_id = self) and
--   become an active member of any family. No production code inserts memberships
--   directly; the only legitimate path is ensure_default_family() (SECURITY
--   DEFINER, bypasses RLS), so dropping the policy breaks nothing.
--
--   When the family-invite feature ships, DO NOT re-add an open self-insert
--   policy: gate joins through a SECURITY DEFINER accept_invite() RPC that
--   verifies a pending invite, and default self-inserts to status 'invited'.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users can insert their own membership" ON public.family_members;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- F3 — Revoke PUBLIC/anon EXECUTE on the two default-seed SECURITY DEFINER
--   functions. Both were callable by anon (default PUBLIC grant);
--   create_default_hierarchy's guard is skipped when auth.uid() IS NULL, letting
--   anon seed rows into empty tenants. Revoking the PUBLIC grant closes the anon
--   path while preserving the authenticated client caller (CategoryService). The
--   guard itself is left intact: it intentionally allows the owner/migration path
--   (auth.uid() IS NULL) to proceed.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.create_default_hierarchy(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.create_default_hierarchy(uuid) TO authenticated;

REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.create_default_categories(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.create_default_categories(uuid) TO authenticated, service_role;

-- related cross-tenant escalations found in the 2026-07-05 and 2026-07-17 audits.
--
-- Covers Security Remediation PRD R2–R5 plus audit findings F1 and F3. R1 (webhook
-- signature enforcement) already shipped in supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts.
--
-- Runs as a single transaction (all-or-nothing). After applying, run the PRD's
-- "Verification (end-to-end)" checks with a throwaway anon-key script — do NOT add
-- committed e2e tests. None of the changes touch storage.objects (which the
-- migration role does not own), so they are safe to run via `supabase db push`.
--
-- Verified before writing: the only caller of insert_receipt_with_context and
-- find_user_by_email is the service-role Resend webhook; create_default_hierarchy is
-- called by an authenticated client (CategoryService); no production code inserts
-- into family_members (default membership is created by the SECURITY DEFINER
-- ensure_default_family(), which bypasses RLS).

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- R2 — Lock down insert_receipt_with_context (fixes C2 + C2b)
--   Pin search_path, add an auth.users existence guard, and restrict EXECUTE to
--   the service role (the webhook's only legitimate caller).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.insert_receipt_with_context(receipt_data jsonb)
 RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path = public
AS $function$
DECLARE
  inserted_receipt jsonb;
  user_id_val uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Extract user_id from the receipt_data
  user_id_val := (receipt_data->>'user_id')::uuid;

  -- Fail closed on a missing or unknown user_id: the caller must not be able to
  -- spoof an arbitrary/nonexistent subject into request.jwt.claims.
  IF user_id_val IS NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'insert_receipt_with_context: user_id is required';
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM auth.users WHERE id = user_id_val) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'insert_receipt_with_context: unknown user_id %', user_id_val;
  END IF;

  -- Set the local auth.uid() for this transaction so triggers that depend on
  -- auth.uid() (e.g. set_receipt_family_id) work.
  PERFORM set_config('request.jwt.claims', json_build_object('sub', user_id_val)::text, true);

  -- NOTE: this insert deliberately mirrors the pre-existing column set. The
  -- separately-tracked "RPC drops suspicious_date / exchange_rate_to_cad" bug is
  -- out of scope for this security migration and is not changed here.
  INSERT INTO receipts (
    user_id,
    receipt_image_path,
    merchant_name,
    total_amount,
    tax,
    transaction_date,
    currency,
    credit_card_name,
    credit_card_last_4
  )
  VALUES (
    user_id_val,
    receipt_data->>'receipt_image_path',
    receipt_data->>'merchant_name',
    (receipt_data->>'total_amount')::numeric,
    (receipt_data->>'tax')::numeric,
    (receipt_data->>'transaction_date')::date,
    receipt_data->>'currency',
    receipt_data->>'credit_card_name',
    receipt_data->>'credit_card_last_4'
  )
  RETURNING to_jsonb(receipts.*) INTO inserted_receipt;

  RETURN inserted_receipt;
END;
$function$;

REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.insert_receipt_with_context(jsonb) FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.insert_receipt_with_context(jsonb) TO service_role;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- R3 — Fix the tautological receipts write checks (fixes C3)
--   The INSERT and UPDATE WITH CHECK clauses used `fm.family_id = fm.family_id`
--   (always true) instead of `fm.family_id = receipts.family_id`, letting any
--   active member of any family write receipts into an arbitrary family_id.
--   The USING clauses / SELECT / DELETE policies were already correct.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated can insert receipts" ON public.receipts;
CREATE POLICY "Authenticated can insert receipts"
ON public.receipts
AS PERMISSIVE
FOR INSERT
TO public
WITH CHECK (
  ((SELECT auth.uid()) IS NOT NULL)
  AND (
    (family_id IS NULL)
    OR EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM family_members fm
      WHERE fm.family_id = receipts.family_id
        AND fm.user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
        AND fm.status = 'active'
    )
  )
);

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Members can update family receipts" ON public.receipts;
CREATE POLICY "Members can update family receipts"
ON public.receipts
AS PERMISSIVE
FOR UPDATE
TO public
USING (
  ((family_id IS NOT NULL) AND EXISTS (
     SELECT 1 FROM family_members fm
     WHERE fm.family_id = receipts.family_id
       AND fm.user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
       AND fm.status = 'active'))
  OR ((family_id IS NULL) AND ((SELECT auth.uid()) = user_id))
)
WITH CHECK (
  ((family_id IS NOT NULL) AND EXISTS (
     SELECT 1 FROM family_members fm
     WHERE fm.family_id = receipts.family_id
       AND fm.user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
       AND fm.status = 'active'))
  OR ((family_id IS NULL) AND ((SELECT auth.uid()) = user_id))
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- R4 — Restrict find_user_by_email to the service role (fixes H1)
--   Already SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path; only the grant is wrong
--   (defaults to PUBLIC). The webhook (service role) is the only caller.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.find_user_by_email(text) TO service_role;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- R5 — Scope family_members reads without RLS recursion (fixes H2)
--   Replace the world-readable USING(true) SELECT policy with a membership-scoped
--   one. A SECURITY DEFINER helper reads family_members as owner, breaking the
--   recursion that USING(true) was papering over.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.is_member_of(target_family uuid)
 RETURNS boolean
 LANGUAGE sql
 STABLE
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path = public
AS $function$
  SELECT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.family_members fm
    WHERE fm.family_id = target_family
      AND fm.user_id = auth.uid()
      AND fm.status = 'active'
  );
$function$;

REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.is_member_of(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.is_member_of(uuid) TO authenticated;

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated users can view family memberships" ON public.family_members;
CREATE POLICY "Members can view family memberships"
ON public.family_members
AS PERMISSIVE
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (
  user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
  OR public.is_member_of(family_id)
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- F1 — Remove the open family_members self-insert policy (fixes cross-tenant join)
--   The policy's WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid()) never verified the family_id,
--   so any authed user could INSERT (family_id = <victim>, user_id = self) and
--   become an active member of any family. No production code inserts memberships
--   directly; the only legitimate path is ensure_default_family() (SECURITY
--   DEFINER, bypasses RLS), so dropping the policy breaks nothing.
--
--   When the family-invite feature ships, DO NOT re-add an open self-insert
--   policy: gate joins through a SECURITY DEFINER accept_invite() RPC that
--   verifies a pending invite, and default self-inserts to status 'invited'.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users can insert their own membership" ON public.family_members;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- F3 — Revoke PUBLIC/anon EXECUTE on the two default-seed SECURITY DEFINER
--   functions. Both were callable by anon (default PUBLIC grant);
--   create_default_hierarchy's guard is skipped when auth.uid() IS NULL, letting
--   anon seed rows into empty tenants. Revoking the PUBLIC grant closes the anon
--   path while preserving the authenticated client caller (CategoryService). The
--   guard itself is left intact: it intentionally allows the owner/migration path
--   (auth.uid() IS NULL) to proceed.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.create_default_hierarchy(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.create_default_hierarchy(uuid) TO authenticated;

REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.create_default_categories(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.create_default_categories(uuid) TO authenticated, service_role;

## F1 — designing "add family members by invitation" (design only)

The secure shape is: **all membership writes go through vetted `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs; there is never an open client INSERT policy on `family_members`.** That's exactly why F1's fix is "drop the self-insert policy" rather than "narrow it."

### Data model — a separate `family_invitations` table
Don't reuse `family_members(status='invited')` for this, because the invitee usually has **no account yet** (no `user_id` to store), and you don't want any membership-derived access to exist before acceptance. Key the invite by **email** instead:

- `id`, `family_id → families`, `invited_email` (normalized lowercase)
- `invited_by → auth.users`, `role` (default `'member'`)
- `token` — a random secret; ideally store a **hash** of it so a DB read can't replay it
- `status` ∈ `pending | accepted | revoked | expired`, `expires_at` (e.g. 7 days)
- `accepted_by`, `accepted_at`

### Flow (three RPCs, all `SECURITY DEFINER`, `search_path` pinned, granted to `authenticated` only, revoked from `PUBLIC`/`anon`)
1. **`invite_to_family(family_id, email, role)`** — verifies the caller is an active member (or `owner`) of that family, inserts a `pending` invite with a random token + expiry, returns the token. The app then emails an invite link `…/invite?token=…` via the existing Resend/notify infra (which already requires a verified sender).
2. **`accept_invite(token)`** — the invitee signs in/up, opens the link. The RPC looks up a `pending`, non-expired invite by token, **requires `auth.users` email == `invited_email`** (blocks link-forwarding hijack — and note it matches the *verified* auth email, not the unverified profile aliases from F2), then inserts `family_members(family_id, auth.uid(), role, 'active')` `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and flips the invite to `accepted`. **This is the only client-driven path that creates an active membership.**
3. **`revoke_invite(id)` / resend** — inviter-only, flips `status`.

### RLS
- `family_members`: no INSERT policy (F1 drop); SELECT stays the R5 `is_member_of` scoped policy. All inserts happen inside the RPCs, which bypass RLS as definer.
- `family_invitations`: SELECT for the inviter / active family members and for the invitee (invite addressed to their email); no direct client INSERT/UPDATE — mutation only through the RPCs.

### Things to get right
- **Token**: random 32-byte value, store hashed, single-use, expiring.
- **Authorization to invite**: enforce active-membership (or an `owner`/`admin` role) *inside* the RPC — don't trust the client.
- **Abuse**: cap pending invites per family; rate-limit sends.
- **Anon**: none of these RPCs granted to `anon`.
- **UI**: a Family settings page (members list + pending invites + "invite by email" + revoke/resend) — this is the backlog's unbuilt **"Family editor"** feature, so the invite work and that page are the same effort.

This pairs naturally with the **F2** fix (verify/uniquify emails), since acceptance keys off the authenticated user's verified email.

input.content:
# PRD — Family Invitations (invite users to join a family)

- **Status:** Draft
- **Created:** 2026-07-17
- **Owner:** _unassigned_
- **Surface:** new `family_invitations` table + `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs
  (`invite_to_family` / `accept_invite` / `revoke_invite`); a new Family settings
  page; the existing email infra (`supabase/functions/_shared/notify.ts`).
- **Related:**
  - Backlog **"Family editor"** feature (this PRD is its concrete design).
  - [Security Remediation PRD](prd-security-remediation.md) **F1** — the open
    `family_members` self-insert policy must be dropped; this feature provides the
    _only_ sanctioned membership-write path that replaces it.
  - Security **F2** (unverified/non-unique profile emails) — acceptance keys off
    the invitee's **verified `auth.users` email**, not profile aliases.
  - [domain-model.md](domain-model.md) — Family, Family Member terminology.

## Terminology

See [domain-model.md](domain-model.md). A **Family** is the data-scoping unit; a
**Family Member** is a row in `family_members(family_id, user_id, role, status,
is_default)` with `role ∈ {owner, member}` and `status ∈ {active, invited,
removed}`. An **Invitation** (new concept) is a pending, email-addressed offer to
join a family; it is **not** a membership and grants no access until accepted. UI
copy uses "invite" / "family member".

## Problem

Today a user only ever belongs to the default family created for them at signup by
`ensure_default_family()`. There is **no way to add another person to a family** —
the "Family editor / invite other users" feature was specced but never built, so
households can't actually share an expense view.

Naively, the missing piece looks like "let a user insert a `family_members` row."
That is exactly the critical **F1** hole: the old `family_members` INSERT policy
(`WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid())`) let any authenticated user self-join **any**
family. The remediation drops that policy, leaving **no** client membership-write
path. This PRD supplies the secure replacement: an invitation flow where every
membership write goes through a vetted `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC.

## Goals

- A family member can invite another person **by email** to their family.
- The invitee accepts via a link and becomes an active member — **only** after a
  server-side check that the invite is valid and addressed to them.
- No path lets a user join a family they weren't invited to (F1 stays closed).
- Members can see and **revoke / resend** pending invitations.

## Non-goals

- **Roles/permissions beyond the existing `owner`/`member`.** No granular
  per-category or read-only roles in v1.
- **Removing members / leaving a family / transferring ownership** — follow-up
  work; this PRD is invite + accept + revoke only.
- **Multi-family switching UI.** Users may end up in >1 family via invites; the
  default-family selection UX is out of scope (they still operate on their default
  family). Flag as an open question.
- **In-app notifications / real-time.** Invites are delivered by email only.
- Fixing F2 itself. This feature _depends_ on verified auth emails but does not
  implement email verification.

## Design

### D1 — `family_invitations` table (invites are keyed by email, not user_id)

An invitee usually has **no account yet**, so there is no `user_id` to store, and
we must not create any membership-derived access before acceptance. Therefore
invitations live in their own table, addressed by email:

| Column          | Notes                                                             |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`            | uuid pk                                                          |
| `family_id`     | → `families(id)` on delete cascade                              |
| `invited_email` | normalized `lower(trim(...))`                                    |
| `invited_by`    | → `auth.users(id)` (the inviter)                                |
| `role`          | `'member'` default (only `owner`/`member` allowed)              |
| `token_hash`    | **hash** of a random secret token (store the hash, not the raw) |
| `status`        | `pending \| accepted \| revoked \| expired`                     |
| `created_at`    | default now()                                                    |
| `expires_at`    | default now() + interval (e.g. 7 days)                          |
| `accepted_by`   | → `auth.users(id)`, null until accepted                        |
| `accepted_at`   | null until accepted                                             |

Partial unique index on `(family_id, invited_email) WHERE status = 'pending'` so a
family can't accumulate duplicate live invites to the same address.

### D2 — Three `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs (the only membership-write path)

All three: `SET search_path = public`, `REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC`, `GRANT
EXECUTE TO authenticated` (never `anon`). They enforce authorization **inside** the
function — never trust the client.

1. **`invite_to_family(p_family_id, p_email, p_role)`** — verify the caller is an
   **active member** of `p_family_id` (later: require `owner`); reject if the email
   already belongs to an active member; insert a `pending` invitation with a fresh
   random token + expiry; return the **raw token once** (never stored). The app
   then sends the invite email (D4). Enforce a per-family pending-invite cap.
2. **`accept_invite(p_token)`** — hash `p_token`, look up a `pending`, non-expired
   invitation; **require `auth.users.email` of `auth.uid()` == `invited_email`**
   (blocks a forwarded/leaked link being redeemed by someone else); insert
   `family_members(family_id, auth.uid(), role, 'active')` `ON CONFLICT DO
   NOTHING`; mark the invite `accepted` (`accepted_by`/`accepted_at`). Idempotent.
3. **`revoke_invite(p_invitation_id)`** — inviter or an active member of the
   family flips `status = 'revoked'`.

A scheduled/opportunistic sweep (or a check inside `accept_invite`) treats
`expires_at < now()` as `expired`.

### D3 — RLS

- `family_members`: **no INSERT policy** (F1). SELECT stays the membership-scoped
  policy (`is_member_of` helper from the remediation). All inserts flow through the
  RPCs, which bypass RLS as definer.
- `family_invitations`: SELECT for (a) active members of `family_id` and (b) the
  invitee (`invited_email = auth.users.email of auth.uid()`), so a user can see
  invites addressed to them. **No** direct client INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy —
  mutation only via the RPCs. `token_hash` must never be exposed to the invitee's
  SELECT (return a redacted view or omit the column from the client query).

### D4 — Email delivery

Reuse `supabase/functions/_shared/notify.ts` (Resend). The invite email contains a
link `…/invite?token=<raw-token>`. Sender must be `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` on a verified
domain (per CLAUDE.md, otherwise Resend 403s). The raw token appears only in the
email and the acceptance URL — never persisted server-side.

### D5 — UI

A **Family** settings page (fulfils the backlog "Family editor"):

- Member list (name/email, role, status).
- "Invite by email" form → `invite_to_family`.
- Pending-invitations list with **Revoke** and **Resend** (resend re-sends the
  email; may rotate the token).
- A public-ish **`/invite?token=…`** landing page: if signed out, prompt sign-in /
  sign-up (carrying the token through auth), then call `accept_invite`; show
  success / expired / wrong-account states.

### D6 — Token security

- Random ≥ 32 bytes; store only a hash (`token_hash`); compare by hashing the
  presented token. A DB read then can't yield a usable link.
- Single-use (status → `accepted`) and time-boxed (`expires_at`).
- Constant-time-ish lookup by hash; generic "invalid or expired" error (don't
  distinguish revoked vs expired vs unknown to the client).

## Requirements

- **R1 — Schema.** Add `family_invitations` (D1) with the partial unique index and
  FKs. Enable RLS.
- **R2 — Invite RPC.** `invite_to_family` (D2.1) with active-member authorization,
  duplicate/active-member rejection, pending-cap, token+expiry, returns raw token.
- **R3 — Accept RPC.** `accept_invite` (D2.2): validate pending+unexpired, **email
  match against verified `auth.users` email**, insert active membership
  idempotently, mark accepted.
- **R4 — Revoke RPC.** `revoke_invite` (D2.3), member-authorized.
- **R5 — RLS (D3).** Invitation SELECT policies for members + invitee; no direct
  client writes; `token_hash` never returned to clients.
- **R6 — Email (D4).** Send the invite link through `notify.ts`; verified sender.
- **R7 — UI (D5).** Family settings page (list/invite/revoke/resend) + `/invite`
  acceptance landing with signed-out→auth→accept handoff.
- **R8 — Grants.** All RPCs `REVOKE FROM PUBLIC`, `GRANT TO authenticated`, pinned
  `search_path`; nothing granted to `anon`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An active member invites `x@example.com`; a `pending` invitation is created and
   an email with a working accept link is sent.
2. A signed-in user **whose verified email is `x@example.com`** opens the link and
   becomes an `active` member; the invitation is `accepted`. Re-clicking is a
   no-op (idempotent), not an error or a second row.
3. A signed-in user with a **different** email opens the same link → rejected, no
   membership created.
4. An expired or revoked link → generic "invalid or expired"; no membership.
5. A user **cannot** join a family without a valid invitation by any route —
   direct `family_members` INSERT via the anon/authenticated client is denied
   (F1 stays closed), and the RPCs reject non-members' invite attempts.
6. Members can list pending invites and revoke/resend them; a non-member cannot.
7. `token_hash` is never returned by any client-visible query.

## Security considerations

- Depends on **F1** (drop open self-insert policy) — this feature is the sanctioned
  replacement. Do not ship one without the other.
- Depends on **verified emails** (F2): the email match in `accept_invite` uses
  `auth.users.email` (verified at signup) — **not** the unverified `profiles`
  aliases — so a hijacked/pre-claimed alias can't redeem an invite.
- `anon` gets **no** grant on any RPC. Authorization is enforced server-side in the
  definer functions, never in the client.
- Token is hashed at rest, single-use, expiring; errors are generic.
- Rate-limit invite creation and email sends per family/inviter to curb spam/abuse.

## Testing notes

Per project convention — unit tests own correctness, Playwright is seam-only:

- **Unit:** pure logic (email normalization, token hashing/verification, expiry
  computation, the accept-state machine: pending→accepted, expired, wrong-email,
  revoked, already-accepted). Keep Supabase/Resend out; mock at the boundary.
- **RLS / RPC behaviour:** the env-gated integration suite (like
  `family-category-visibility.spec.ts`, run against `supabase start`) is the right
  home for "non-member can't invite", "wrong-email accept denied", "direct insert
  denied" — these can't be unit-tested. Not run in CI.
- **Playwright seam:** one thin flow proving the `/invite` page is wired
  (token → accept RPC → membership), not a matrix.
- No committed test may send real email or hit Resend.

## Open questions

1. **Multi-family UX.** Once a user can belong to >1 family, how do they choose/see
   the active one? (`is_default` exists; a switcher is out of scope here — decide
   whether v1 simply keeps the default family and defers switching.)
2. **Owner-only invites?** v1 allows any active member to invite. Restrict to
   `owner` (and add member-management) now, or later?
3. **Invite a not-yet-registered user.** The email match requires the invitee to
   sign up with that exact address first. Acceptable, or do we need a "claim on
   signup" path that auto-links a pending invite when a new account verifies a
   matching email?
4. **Resend token rotation.** Does "Resend" reuse the token or issue a new one

# PRD — Family Invitations (invite users to join a family)

- **Status:** Draft
- **Created:** 2026-07-17
- **Owner:** _unassigned_
- **Surface:** new `family_invitations` table + `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs
  (`invite_to_family` / `accept_invite` / `revoke_invite`); a new Family settings
  page; the existing email infra (`supabase/functions/_shared/notify.ts`).
- **Related:**
  - Backlog **"Family editor"** feature (this PRD is its concrete design).
  - [Security Remediation PRD](prd-security-remediation.md) **F1** — the open
    `family_members` self-insert policy must be dropped; this feature provides the
    _only_ sanctioned membership-write path that replaces it.
  - Security **F2** (unverified/non-unique profile emails) — acceptance keys off
    the invitee's **verified `auth.users` email**, not profile aliases.
  - [domain-model.md](domain-model.md) — Family, Family Member terminology.

## Terminology

See [domain-model.md](domain-model.md). A **Family** is the data-scoping unit; a
**Family Member** is a row in `family_members(family_id, user_id, role, status,
is_default)` with `role ∈ {owner, member}` and `status ∈ {active, invited,
removed}`. An **Invitation** (new concept) is a pending, email-addressed offer to
join a family; it is **not** a membership and grants no access until accepted. UI
copy uses "invite" / "family member".

## Problem

Today a user only ever belongs to the default family created for them at signup by
`ensure_default_family()`. There is **no way to add another person to a family** —
the "Family editor / invite other users" feature was specced but never built, so
households can't actually share an expense view.

Naively, the missing piece looks like "let a user insert a `family_members` row."
That is exactly the critical **F1** hole: the old `family_members` INSERT policy
(`WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid())`) let any authenticated user self-join **any**
family. The remediation drops that policy, leaving **no** client membership-write
path. This PRD supplies the secure replacement: an invitation flow where every
membership write goes through a vetted `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC.

## Goals

- A family member can invite another person **by email** to their family.
- The invitee accepts via a link and becomes an active member — **only** after a
  server-side check that the invite is valid and addressed to them.
- No path lets a user join a family they weren't invited to (F1 stays closed).
- Members can see and **revoke / resend** pending invitations.

## Non-goals

- **Roles/permissions beyond the existing `owner`/`member`.** No granular
  per-category or read-only roles in v1.
- **Removing members / leaving a family / transferring ownership** — follow-up
  work; this PRD is invite + accept + revoke only.
- **Multi-family switching UI.** Users may end up in >1 family via invites; the
  default-family selection UX is out of scope (they still operate on their default
  family). Flag as an open question.
- **In-app notifications / real-time.** Invites are delivered by email only.
- Fixing F2 itself. This feature _depends_ on verified auth emails but does not
  implement email verification.

## Design

### D1 — `family_invitations` table (invites are keyed by email, not user_id)

An invitee usually has **no account yet**, so there is no `user_id` to store, and
we must not create any membership-derived access before acceptance. Therefore
invitations live in their own table, addressed by email:

| Column          | Notes                                                             |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`            | uuid pk                                                          |
| `family_id`     | → `families(id)` on delete cascade                              |
| `invited_email` | normalized `lower(trim(...))`                                    |
| `invited_by`    | → `auth.users(id)` (the inviter)                                |
| `role`          | `'member'` default (only `owner`/`member` allowed)              |
| `token_hash`    | **hash** of a random secret token (store the hash, not the raw) |
| `status`        | `pending \| accepted \| revoked \| expired`                     |
| `created_at`    | default now()                                                    |
| `expires_at`    | default now() + interval (e.g. 7 days)                          |
| `accepted_by`   | → `auth.users(id)`, null until accepted                        |
| `accepted_at`   | null until accepted                                             |

Partial unique index on `(family_id, invited_email) WHERE status = 'pending'` so a
family can't accumulate duplicate live invites to the same address.

### D2 — Three `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs (the only membership-write path)

All three: `SET search_path = public`, `REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC`, `GRANT
EXECUTE TO authenticated` (never `anon`). They enforce authorization **inside** the
function — never trust the client.

1. **`invite_to_family(p_family_id, p_email, p_role)`** — verify the caller is an
   **active member** of `p_family_id` (later: require `owner`); reject if the email
   already belongs to an active member; insert a `pending` invitation with a fresh
   random token + expiry; return the **raw token once** (never stored). The app
   then sends the invite email (D4). Enforce a per-family pending-invite cap.
2. **`accept_invite(p_token)`** — hash `p_token`, look up a `pending`, non-expired
   invitation; **require `auth.users.email` of `auth.uid()` == `invited_email`**
   (blocks a forwarded/leaked link being redeemed by someone else); insert
   `family_members(family_id, auth.uid(), role, 'active')` `ON CONFLICT DO
   NOTHING`; mark the invite `accepted` (`accepted_by`/`accepted_at`). Idempotent.
3. **`revoke_invite(p_invitation_id)`** — inviter or an active member of the
   family flips `status = 'revoked'`.

A scheduled/opportunistic sweep (or a check inside `accept_invite`) treats
`expires_at < now()` as `expired`.

### D3 — RLS

- `family_members`: **no INSERT policy** (F1). SELECT stays the membership-scoped
  policy (`is_member_of` helper from the remediation). All inserts flow through the
  RPCs, which bypass RLS as definer.
- `family_invitations`: SELECT for (a) active members of `family_id` and (b) the
  invitee (`invited_email = auth.users.email of auth.uid()`), so a user can see
  invites addressed to them. **No** direct client INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy —
  mutation only via the RPCs. `token_hash` must never be exposed to the invitee's
  SELECT (return a redacted view or omit the column from the client query).

### D4 — Email delivery

Reuse `supabase/functions/_shared/notify.ts` (Resend). The invite email contains a
link `…/invite?token=<raw-token>`. Sender must be `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` on a verified
domain (per CLAUDE.md, otherwise Resend 403s). The raw token appears only in the
email and the acceptance URL — never persisted server-side.

### D5 — UI

A **Family** settings page (fulfils the backlog "Family editor"):

- Member list (name/email, role, status).
- "Invite by email" form → `invite_to_family`.
- Pending-invitations list with **Revoke** and **Resend** (resend re-sends the
  email; may rotate the token).
- A public-ish **`/invite?token=…`** landing page: if signed out, prompt sign-in /
  sign-up (carrying the token through auth), then call `accept_invite`; show
  success / expired / wrong-account states.

### D6 — Token security

- Random ≥ 32 bytes; store only a hash (`token_hash`); compare by hashing the
  presented token. A DB read then can't yield a usable link.
- Single-use (status → `accepted`) and time-boxed (`expires_at`).
- Constant-time-ish lookup by hash; generic "invalid or expired" error (don't
  distinguish revoked vs expired vs unknown to the client).

## Requirements

- **R1 — Schema.** Add `family_invitations` (D1) with the partial unique index and
  FKs. Enable RLS.
- **R2 — Invite RPC.** `invite_to_family` (D2.1) with active-member authorization,
  duplicate/active-member rejection, pending-cap, token+expiry, returns raw token.
- **R3 — Accept RPC.** `accept_invite` (D2.2): validate pending+unexpired, **email
  match against verified `auth.users` email**, insert active membership
  idempotently, mark accepted.
- **R4 — Revoke RPC.** `revoke_invite` (D2.3), member-authorized.
- **R5 — RLS (D3).** Invitation SELECT policies for members + invitee; no direct
  client writes; `token_hash` never returned to clients.
- **R6 — Email (D4).** Send the invite link through `notify.ts`; verified sender.
- **R7 — UI (D5).** Family settings page (list/invite/revoke/resend) + `/invite`
  acceptance landing with signed-out→auth→accept handoff.
- **R8 — Grants.** All RPCs `REVOKE FROM PUBLIC`, `GRANT TO authenticated`, pinned
  `search_path`; nothing granted to `anon`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An active member invites `x@example.com`; a `pending` invitation is created and
   an email with a working accept link is sent.
2. A signed-in user **whose verified email is `x@example.com`** opens the link and
   becomes an `active` member; the invitation is `accepted`. Re-clicking is a
   no-op (idempotent), not an error or a second row.
3. A signed-in user with a **different** email opens the same link → rejected, no
   membership created.
4. An expired or revoked link → generic "invalid or expired"; no membership.
5. A user **cannot** join a family without a valid invitation by any route —
   direct `family_members` INSERT via the anon/authenticated client is denied
   (F1 stays closed), and the RPCs reject non-members' invite attempts.
6. Members can list pending invites and revoke/resend them; a non-member cannot.
7. `token_hash` is never returned by any client-visible query.

## Security considerations

- Depends on **F1** (drop open self-insert policy) — this feature is the sanctioned
  replacement. Do not ship one without the other.
- Depends on **verified emails** (F2): the email match in `accept_invite` uses
  `auth.users.email` (verified at signup) — **not** the unverified `profiles`
  aliases — so a hijacked/pre-claimed alias can't redeem an invite.
- `anon` gets **no** grant on any RPC. Authorization is enforced server-side in the
  definer functions, never in the client.
- Token is hashed at rest, single-use, expiring; errors are generic.
- Rate-limit invite creation and email sends per family/inviter to curb spam/abuse.

## Testing notes

Per project convention — unit tests own correctness, Playwright is seam-only:

- **Unit:** pure logic (email normalization, token hashing/verification, expiry
  computation, the accept-state machine: pending→accepted, expired, wrong-email,
  revoked, already-accepted). Keep Supabase/Resend out; mock at the boundary.
- **RLS / RPC behaviour:** the env-gated integration suite (like
  `family-category-visibility.spec.ts`, run against `supabase start`) is the right
  home for "non-member can't invite", "wrong-email accept denied", "direct insert
  denied" — these can't be unit-tested. Not run in CI.
- **Playwright seam:** one thin flow proving the `/invite` page is wired
  (token → accept RPC → membership), not a matrix.
- No committed test may send real email or hit Resend.

## Open questions

1. **Multi-family UX.** Once a user can belong to >1 family, how do they choose/see
   the active one? (`is_default` exists; a switcher is out of scope here — decide
   whether v1 simply keeps the default family and defers switching.)
2. **Owner-only invites?** v1 allows any active member to invite. Restrict to
   `owner` (and add member-management) now, or later?
3. **Invite a not-yet-registered user.** The email match requires the invitee to
   sign up with that exact address first. Acceptable, or do we need a "claim on
   signup" path that auto-links a pending invite when a new account verifies a
   matching email?
4. **Resend token rotation.** Does "Resend" reuse the token or issue a new one
   (invalidating the old link)? Recommend rotate.
5. **Cross-link with F2.** Should this PRD wait on the F2 email-verification/
   uniqueness work, or can it ship against `auth.users` emails alone (which are
   already verified)? Recommend the latter — it only reads verified auth emails.

## Sequencing

1. Land **F1** (drop the open self-insert policy) — prerequisite.
2. **R1** schema → **R2–R4** RPCs → **R5** RLS → **R8** grants (the secure core;
   verifiable via the integration suite before any UI).
3. **R6** email, then **R7** UI (settings page + `/invite` landing).
4. Seam test; docs (`domain-model.md` gains "Invitation").

Each of steps 1–3 is independently reviewable and leaves the app no less secure.

Great — since it's live, you can verify two separate things: (1) you didn't lock out legitimate use, and (2) the holes are actually closed. Do both.

## 1. Fastest signal — the app still works (regression)
Log into the live app and confirm normal use, because two of the changes touched paths real users hit:
- **Expenses / Receipts / Spending pages load *your* data.** These read `family_members` through RLS — if R5 (the new scoped SELECT policy + `is_member_of` helper) were wrong, family-scoped pages would show *no* rows or error. Seeing your receipts = R5 didn't break legit reads.
- **Create a category** (e.g. via the Spending hierarchy editor). That calls `create_default_hierarchy` as an authenticated user — if F3's REVOKE went too far, this would fail. It working = F3 kept the authenticated caller.
- **Forward a receipt email** and confirm it still ingests. That's the service-role webhook path through `insert_receipt_with_context` / `find_user_by_email` (R2/R4) — proves the REVOKE didn't cut off the one legitimate caller.

If all three behave normally, the migration didn't regress anything.

## 2. Confirm the holes are closed (the actual point)
The app UI will never make these calls, so you test with the **public anon key** directly — this is the PRD's throwaway-verification step. Grab your `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` from the live app's **DevTools → Network** (any Supabase request shows both in the headers/URL) or from your `.env`. Then:

```bash

ANON="<public anon key>"
H=(-H "apikey: $ANON" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANON" -H "Content-Type: application/json")

# R4 — email enumeration (chain step H1)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST "$URL/rest/v1/rpc/find_user_by_email" "${H[@]}" \
  -d '{"email_address":"anybody@example.com"}'

# R2 — receipt forgery (chain step C2)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST "$URL/rest/v1/rpc/insert_receipt_with_context" "${H[@]}" \
  -d '{"receipt_data":{"user_id":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000","merchant_name":"x","total_amount":1}}'

# F3 — anon seed functions
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST "$URL/rest/v1/rpc/create_default_hierarchy"  "${H[@]}" -d '{"p_family_id":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"}'
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Throwaway verification for the 2026-07-17 security remediation migration
# (supabase/migrations/20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql: R2–R5, F1, F3).
#
# Runs against the LIVE deployment using the PUBLIC anon key (and, optionally, a
# logged-in user's JWT). It only makes calls that SHOULD be denied — nothing is
# written when the migration is working. NOT committed (.scratch/ is gitignored);
# do not turn this into an e2e test (see prd-security-remediation.md §Verification).
#
# Usage:
#   export SUPABASE_URL="https://<ref>.supabase.co"
#   export SUPABASE_ANON_KEY="<public anon key>"          # from DevTools > Network or .env
#   # optional — enables the authenticated cross-tenant checks (F1, R5):
#   export SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN="<a logged-in user's JWT>"  # the Bearer token on any authed request
#   # optional — enables the webhook check (R1):
#   export RESEND_FUNCTION_URL="https://<ref>.functions.supabase.co/resend"
#   ./.scratch/verify-security.sh
#
# This script deliberately does NOT read .env (it is a 1Password FIFO — sourcing it
# can block). Export the two vars yourself.

set -uo pipefail

: "${SUPABASE_URL:?export SUPABASE_URL first}"
: "${SUPABASE_ANON_KEY:?export SUPABASE_ANON_KEY first}"
SUPABASE_URL="${SUPABASE_URL%/}" # strip trailing slash

green=$'\e[32m'; red=$'\e[31m'; dim=$'\e[2m'; yel=$'\e[33m'; rst=$'\e[0m'
pass_n=0; fail_n=0

pass() { printf '  %sPASS%s %s\n' "$green" "$rst" "$1"; pass_n=$((pass_n + 1)); }
fail() { printf '  %sFAIL%s %s\n' "$red"   "$rst" "$1"; fail_n=$((fail_n + 1)); }
note() { printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$dim" "$1" "$rst"; }

# req METHOD URL DATA BEARER  -> prints "<body>\n<http_code>"
req() {
	local method="$1" url="$2" data="$3" bearer="$4"
	curl -s -w $'\n%{http_code}' -X "$method" "$url" \
		-H "apikey: $SUPABASE_ANON_KEY" \
		-H "Authorization: Bearer $bearer" \
		-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
		${data:+--data "$data"}
}

# Passes when the call is rejected with 401/403 (permission denied / RLS).
assert_denied() {
	local label="$1" method="$2" path="$3" data="$4" bearer="${5:-$SUPABASE_ANON_KEY}"
	local resp code body
	resp="$(req "$method" "$SUPABASE_URL$path" "$data" "$bearer")"
	code="$(tail -n1 <<<"$resp")"; body="$(sed '$d' <<<"$resp" | tr -d '\n' | cut -c1-180)"
	if [[ "$code" == "401" || "$code" == "403" ]]; then
		pass "$label — denied ($code)"
	else
		fail "$label — expected 401/403, got $code ${dim}${body}${rst}"
	fi
}

# Passes on any non-2xx (row not created). Used where a FK error (4xx/409) is also
# an acceptable "not written" outcome.
assert_rejected() {
	local label="$1" method="$2" path="$3" data="$4" bearer="${5:-$SUPABASE_ANON_KEY}"
	local resp code body
	resp="$(req "$method" "$SUPABASE_URL$path" "$data" "$bearer")"
	code="$(tail -n1 <<<"$resp")"; body="$(sed '$d' <<<"$resp" | tr -d '\n' | cut -c1-180)"
	if [[ "$code" =~ ^2 ]]; then
		fail "$label — NOT rejected, got $code ${dim}${body}${rst}"
	else
		pass "$label — rejected ($code)"
	fi
}

ZERO="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"

echo
echo "== Anon-key checks (no login) =="
note "Each should be permission-denied. A 200 here means the hole is still open."
assert_denied "R4  find_user_by_email (chain H1)" \
	POST /rest/v1/rpc/find_user_by_email \
	'{"email_address":"anybody@example.com"}'
assert_denied "R2  insert_receipt_with_context (chain C2)" \
	POST /rest/v1/rpc/insert_receipt_with_context \
	"{\"receipt_data\":{\"user_id\":\"$ZERO\",\"merchant_name\":\"verify\",\"total_amount\":1}}"
assert_denied "F3  create_default_hierarchy (anon seed)" \
	POST /rest/v1/rpc/create_default_hierarchy \
	"{\"p_family_id\":\"$ZERO\"}"
assert_denied "F3  create_default_categories (anon seed)" \
	POST /rest/v1/rpc/create_default_categories \
	"{\"p_family_id\":\"$ZERO\"}"

echo
echo "== Authenticated cross-tenant checks =="
if [[ -n "${SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
	# F1 — self-insert into an arbitrary family must be rejected (no INSERT policy).
	assert_rejected "F1  family_members self-insert (arbitrary family)" \
		POST /rest/v1/family_members \
		"{\"family_id\":\"$ZERO\",\"user_id\":\"$ZERO\",\"status\":\"active\"}" \
		"$SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN"

	# R5 — you should see only your own + co-member rows, not the whole graph.
	echo "  ${yel}R5${rst}  family_members visible to you (manual review — expect only your family/families):"
	resp="$(req GET "$SUPABASE_URL/rest/v1/family_members?select=family_id,user_id,status" "" "$SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN")"
	code="$(tail -n1 <<<"$resp")"; body="$(sed '$d' <<<"$resp")"
	fams="$(grep -oE '"family_id":"[^"]+"' <<<"$body" | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
	rows="$(grep -oc '"user_id"' <<<"$body")"
	note "HTTP $code — $rows row(s) across $fams distinct family_id(s). If that's more than your own household, R5 did not take."
	note "R3 (cross-family receipt UPDATE) is not auto-tested — verify manually: try to PATCH a receipt's family_id to a family you're not in; expect 403."
else
	note "SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN not set — skipping F1/R5. Grab a JWT from DevTools > Network (the Bearer on any authed request) and re-run to include them."
fi

echo
echo "== Webhook (R1) =="
if [[ -n "${RESEND_FUNCTION_URL:-}" ]]; then
	code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$RESEND_FUNCTION_URL" \
		-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
		--data '{"type":"email.received","data":{}}')"
	if [[ "$code" == "401" ]]; then
		pass "R1  forged/unsigned webhook rejected (401)"
	elif [[ "$code" == "500" ]]; then
		fail "R1  got 500 — RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured in the deployed function"
	else
		fail "R1  expected 401, got $code (fail-open? check handler.ts signature enforcement)"
	fi
else
	note "RESEND_FUNCTION_URL not set — skipping R1. (A genuine forwarded receipt still ingesting is the positive check.)"
fi

echo
echo "== Summary =="
printf '  %s%d passed%s, %s%d failed%s\n' "$green" "$pass_n" "$rst" "$( ((fail_n)) && echo "$red" || echo "$dim")" "$fail_n" "$rst"
if ((fail_n)); then
	note "Any FAIL that returned 200 means that fix is not live. Confirm with: supabase migration list"
	exit 1
fi
echo "  All executed checks passed."

# logged-in user's JWT). It only makes calls that SHOULD be denied — nothing is

#

#   export SUPABASE_URL="https://<ref>.supabase.co"

: "${SUPABASE_ANON_KEY:?export SUPABASE_ANON_KEY first}"

green=$'\e[32m'; red=$'\e[31m'; dim=$'\e[2m'; yel=$'\e[33m'; rst=$'\e[0m'

pass() { printf '  %sPASS%s %s\n' "$green" "$rst" "$1"; pass_n=$((pass_n + 1)); }

if ((fail_n)); then
	note "Any FAIL that returned 200 means that fix is not live. Confirm with: supabase migration list"
	exit 1
fi
echo "  All executed checks passed."

Confirmed the root cause. This is a real miss in the migration — flagging it clearly.

## F3 is still open — the REVOKE was insufficient
**Why:** Supabase applies `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES … GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS TO anon, authenticated` at the platform level, so every function created in `public` gets a **direct grant to `anon`** — not one inherited through `PUBLIC`. My F3 lines only did `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC`, which doesn't remove that direct `anon` grant. That's exactly why **R2/R4 passed but F3 failed**: for those I revoked `FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated` explicitly; for F3 I only revoked `FROM PUBLIC`.

The `409 / 23503` proves it — anon's permission check *passed*, the body ran, and only the foreign-key constraint (nonexistent family) stopped the write. Against a real empty family's id, anon could seed rows.

## The fix (one follow-up migration — the pushed one can't be edited in place)
Since `20260717_…` is already applied on remote, it needs a *new* migration:

```sql
-- 20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql
-- The earlier REVOKE ... FROM PUBLIC missed Supabase's direct anon grant
-- (default privileges grant EXECUTE on public functions straight to anon).
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.create_default_hierarchy(uuid)  FROM anon;
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.create_default_categories(uuid) FROM anon;
```
`authenticated` keeps its explicit grant (lines 200/203), so the `CategoryService` caller is unaffected. After `supabase db push`, re-run the verify script — the two F3 checks should flip to `PASS` (permission-denied *before* any FK check).

## Where things stand

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| R2 insert_receipt_with_context | ✅ denied |
| R4 find_user_by_email | ✅ denied |
| R1 forged webhook | ✅ 401 |
| **F3 seed functions** | ❌ **still anon-executable — needs the follow-up above** |
| F1 self-insert / R3 cross-family / R5 read-scope | ⏳ not yet tested (need a logged-in JWT) |

Two things worth doing next: (1) apply that follow-up and re-verify F3, and (2) run the script again with `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` set so F1/R3/R5 are actually exercised — right now those three are unverified.

That `401` is the tell — and it's not R5 misbehaving. Here's what happened:

## Diagnosis: your JWT was rejected, so the authed checks never actually authenticated
- **401 = the token was *provided but rejected*** (expired or malformed). If the token were simply *missing*, the request would fall back to the `anon` role and return **`200` with `[]`** (RLS filters rows) — not a 401. So the script *did* send your Bearer token; PostgREST just refused it.
- That means the request ran as *unauthenticated*, so **both F1 and R5 tested nothing about your logged-in access.** A valid token reading your own memberships would return `200` with **≥1 row** (your household) — which is the "more than 0" you correctly expected.
- ⚠️ **F1's result is a false pass here** — `assert_rejected` treats the 401 as "rejected," but it was rejected by *auth*, not by the F1 policy. Don't trust F1 until you re-run with a working token.

## Most likely cause: a stale token
Supabase access tokens expire after ~1 hour. Either it aged out, or it got copied with a stray `Bearer ` prefix / quotes / newline.

**Grab a fresh one:**
- DevTools → **Application → Local Storage** → the `sb-<ref>-auth-token` entry → copy the **`access_token`** value, **or**
- **Network** tab → a request that *just succeeded* → copy the `Authorization` header and **strip the leading `Bearer `**.

It must be the bare JWT — three dot-separated segments (`eyJ….eyJ….sig`), no `Bearer `, no quotes. Then re-run within the hour:
```bash
op run --env-file=.env -- env SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN="eyJ...your.jwt...here" ./.scratch/verify-security.sh
```

## The real R5 proof you already have
The definitive "R5 didn't break legitimate reads" check isn't the script — it's the **live app still showing your receipts/expenses** after the push (those pages read `family_members` through the R5 policy). If your data still loads in the app, R5 is fine for legit use; the script's 401 is purely a token issue.
