# PRD — Security Remediation: Unauthenticated Data-Forgery Chain

**Status:** In progress — R1 DONE; **R2–R5 OPEN (critical, unshipped)**
**Date:** 2026-07-05
**Severity:** Critical — unauthenticated cross-user data write, reachable with only the public anon key

> **⚠️ Status verification (2026-07-17):** only **R1** (webhook signature
> enforcement) is implemented — and it landed as a side effect of the Resend
> handler-testability work, not this PRD. It lives in
> `supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts` (fail-closed 401 on bad signature, 500 on
> unset secret). **R2, R3, R4, and R5 are all still unimplemented** — no migration
> dated after this PRD (2026-07-05) touches the audited functions/policies. The
> core unauthenticated chain is therefore **still live in production**:
> `find_user_by_email` is still PUBLIC-executable (H1), `family_members` SELECT is
> still `USING (true)` (H2), `insert_receipt_with_context` is still granted to
> `anon` with no `search_path` pin (C2/C2b), and the `receipts` INSERT/UPDATE
> `WITH CHECK` is still the tautological `fm.family_id = fm.family_id` (C3).
> Closing R1 shut the webhook entry point but not the anon-key path. R2–R5 are four
> small, independent migrations — build them together and re-run the §"Verification
> (end-to-end)" checks before marking Done.
**Surfaces:**

- `supabase/functions/resend/index.ts` (webhook auth)
- `supabase/migrations/` (RLS policies + SECURITY DEFINER RPCs)
- `src/routes/api/ocr/+server.ts`, `src/routes/api/ocr/extract/+server.ts` (OCR endpoints)
  **Source:** Security audit, 2026-07-05 (this session). All findings verified against source.

## Terminology

See `CLAUDE.md`. In short: **RLS** (Row Level Security) is the app's _only_ real
access control — there is no `hooks.server.ts` and no `+page.server.ts` load
guard, so the client route gate in `+layout.svelte` is cosmetic. The
**anon key** (`PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) ships in the browser bundle and must be
treated as public/attacker-held. **Service role** bypasses RLS entirely and is
used only by the Resend edge function. A **family** is the data-scoping unit;
users join families via `family_members`.

## Problem

Five independent defects combine into one unauthenticated attack chain. Each is
real on its own; together they let anyone with the public anon key (or the
webhook URL) forge receipts into any user's account without logging in.

### The chain

```
  Attacker knows only: a victim's email address + the public anon key
        │
        ▼
  [H1] rpc('find_user_by_email', {email})   ── email → victim user UUID
        │   (SECURITY DEFINER, no REVOKE → callable by anon/PUBLIC)
        ▼
  [H2] select * from family_members          ── UUID → victim's family_id
        │   (RLS policy is USING(true) → world-readable to any auth user)
        ▼
  [C2] rpc('insert_receipt_with_context',    ── forge receipt AS the victim
        {receipt_data:{user_id: <victim UUID>, ...}})
        │   (SECURITY DEFINER granted to anon; trusts caller-supplied user_id;
        │    spoofs request.jwt.claims.sub → inserts bypassing RLS)
        ▼
  Forged receipt lands in victim's account / family.
```

Two more defects widen the blast radius:

- **[C1]** The Resend webhook (`resend/index.ts`) is a _second, independent_
  entry point to the same forgery: its signature check is disabled (fail-open),
  so a forged `email.received` POST triggers a service-role receipt insert for
  any `from:` address — no anon key needed at all.
- **[C3]** The `receipts` INSERT/UPDATE RLS check is tautological
  (`fm.family_id = fm.family_id`), so even a _logged-in_ user can write receipts
  into another family's scope directly, without any RPC.

### Confirmed defects

| ID  | File:line                                                                | Defect                                                                                                                                  | Effect                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| C1  | `supabase/functions/resend/index.ts:316-322`                             | Webhook signature failure logs but does **not** return 401 (`return jsonResponse(401,…)` is commented out) — fail-open                  | Anyone who knows the function URL forges `email.received` events → service-role receipt inserts, Mistral cost, attacker-controlled attachment fetches, outbound emails |
| C2  | `003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql:94`                                          | `insert_receipt_with_context` `GRANT EXECUTE … TO … anon`; SECURITY DEFINER reads `user_id` from its JSONB arg and spoofs the JWT claim | Anon-key holder forges receipts attributed to any user, RLS bypassed                                                                                                   |
| C3  | `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql:347` (INSERT) & `:370` (UPDATE)        | `WITH CHECK` contains `fm.family_id = fm.family_id` (always true) instead of `fm.family_id = receipts.family_id`                        | Any authenticated family member writes/moves receipts into any other family's `family_id`                                                                              |
| H1  | `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql:204` (and `002_profiles_table.sql:52`) | `find_user_by_email` SECURITY DEFINER has **no** `GRANT/REVOKE` → defaults to `EXECUTE` for `PUBLIC`                                    | Anon-key holder enumerates registered emails → user UUIDs (input for C2)                                                                                               |
| H2  | `20260114_simple_family_members_policy.sql:16`                           | `family_members` SELECT policy is `USING (true)`                                                                                        | Any authenticated user reads the entire family/membership graph → `family_id` values (input for C3)                                                                    |

### Contributing weakness (not in the core chain)

- **C2b** — the later redefinition of `insert_receipt_with_context` in
  `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql:238` dropped the original's `SET search_path`
  pin and its `auth.users` existence guard. Unpinned `search_path` on a SECURITY
  DEFINER function is a privilege-escalation vector (schema shadowing of
  unqualified table names).

## Goals

- Collapse the unauthenticated chain: **no path** from "public anon key + an
  email address" to writing another user's data.
- Close the second (webhook) entry point so only genuinely Resend-signed events
  are processed.
- Fix the tautological `receipts` write check so cross-family writes are rejected.
- Do all of the above without breaking the legitimate webhook receipt-ingestion
  flow (the only intended caller of both RPCs).

## Non-goals

- Adding server-side auth (`hooks.server.ts` / load guards). Out of scope here;
  RLS-as-sole-control is the current design. Tracked separately (see Open
  questions).
- The Medium/Low findings from the audit (secret logging M1, `/admin/resize-images`
  authz M2, unbounded `families` insert M3, `xlsx` CVEs M4, OCR-endpoint SSRF H3).
  These are real but are their own work items — listed under "Deferred" below so
  the chain fix stays shippable and reviewable on its own.
- Spec-traceability `#{#id}` tags (that system is retired — plain doc only).

## Requirements

Each requirement is a self-contained migration or edit. They are independent and
can land in any order, but **all five** are required to break the chain.

### R1 — Re-enable webhook signature enforcement (fixes C1)

- In `supabase/functions/resend/index.ts`, restore the rejection: on
  `verifyWebhookSignature(...) === false`, `return jsonResponse(401, { error: 'Invalid webhook signature' })`
  (uncomment line 322; remove the "TEMPORARILY ALLOWING" branch at 316–320).
- Make the secret **required**: if `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset, return `500`
  and do not process the event (today an unset secret silently disables
  verification — line 326–328). Fail-closed.
- Verify `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is configured in the deployed function's env
  before shipping, or every real webhook 401s.

### R2 — Lock down `insert_receipt_with_context` (fixes C2, C2b)

- New migration: `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION insert_receipt_with_context(jsonb) FROM anon, authenticated, PUBLIC;`
  then `GRANT EXECUTE … TO service_role;`. The webhook (service role) is the only
  legitimate caller.
- Re-add `SET search_path = public` (or `= ''` with fully-qualified names) to the
  function definition, and restore the `auth.users` existence guard on
  `user_id_val`.
- Regression check: confirm the webhook path still inserts (it uses service role,
  which retains the grant). The client never calls this RPC directly — verify with
  `git grep insert_receipt_with_context src/`.

### R3 — Fix the tautological receipts write check (fixes C3)

- New migration: drop and recreate the `receipts` INSERT and UPDATE policies,
  replacing `fm.family_id = fm.family_id` with `fm.family_id = receipts.family_id`
  in both `WITH CHECK` clauses. Match the already-correct SELECT/DELETE policies
  (`:357`, `:380`).
- Preserve the existing `(family_id IS NULL AND auth.uid() = user_id)` branch so
  personal (no-family) receipts still write.
- Regression check: a user in family A can no longer insert/update a receipt with
  `family_id` = family B; a user can still create receipts in their own family and
  personal receipts.

### R4 — Restrict `find_user_by_email` to service role (fixes H1)

- New migration: `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION find_user_by_email(text) FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated;`
  then `GRANT EXECUTE … TO service_role;`.
- Regression check: the webhook (`resend/index.ts:353`) still resolves senders
  (service role). Confirm no client code calls it (`git grep find_user_by_email src/`).

### R5 — Scope `family_members` reads without RLS recursion (fixes H2)

- Replace the `USING (true)` SELECT policy (`20260114`) with a scoped one that
  does **not** re-query `family_members` in its own predicate (the original
  recursion bug that `USING(true)` was papering over).
- Recommended approach: a `SECURITY DEFINER` helper
  `is_member_of(target_family uuid) returns boolean` that reads `family_members`
  as definer (breaking the recursion), then policy
  `USING (user_id = auth.uid() OR is_member_of(family_id))`. Pin the helper's
  `search_path` and grant it to `authenticated`.
- Regression check: a user sees their own memberships and co-members of families
  they belong to, but **not** arbitrary other families' rows. Verify the
  `20260113`/`20260114` recursion does not reappear (load any family-scoped page).

## Verification (end-to-end)

The chain is broken when **all** of these hold in the deployed environment:

1. `rpc('find_user_by_email', …)` with the anon key returns permission-denied (R4).
2. `select from family_members` with the anon key / a foreign family returns only
   the caller's own + co-member rows (R5).
3. `rpc('insert_receipt_with_context', …)` with the anon key returns
   permission-denied (R2).
4. An authenticated user's attempt to INSERT/UPDATE a receipt with a foreign

Verify with the PRD's throwaway anon-key script — do NOT commit e2e tests. **Schedule ahead of feature work.**
33	- **🔴 CRITICAL SECURITY — any authed user can self-join any family (full cross-tenant breach).** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit, verified against source.)_ The `family_members` INSERT policy `"Users can insert their own membership"` (`supabase/migrations/20251010000319_remote_schema.sql:324-329`) has `WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid())` — it checks only that you insert **your own** user_id, never that the `family_id` is yours or that an invite exists; `status` defaults to `'active'`. Combined with the world-readable `family_members` SELECT (`USING(true)`, lets you enumerate every `family_id`), any logged-in user can `INSERT (family_id=<victim>, user_id=self)` and become an active member of any family — then every family-scoped policy (receipts, transactions, categories, storage objects, etc.) grants full read/write to that tenant's financial data + receipt images. One request, whole-app tenant breach. **Distinct from the R2–R5 chain above** (which is about the RPCs and reading memberships; this is the self-service *write* into an arbitrary family). Fix: gate membership INSERT behind a verified invite (e.g. an `accept_invite` SECURITY DEFINER RPC), default self-inserts to `'invited'`, and drop the open self-insert policy. Should land with the R2–R5 migration pass. **Highest priority.**
34	- **🟠 HIGH SECURITY — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint** (`002_profiles_table.sql`). The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
35	- **🟡 MEDIUM SECURITY — two more SECURITY DEFINER functions are PUBLIC/anon-executable.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit, verified.)_ `create_default_hierarchy(uuid)` and `create_default_categories(...)` (`20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql`, `20260111000001_migrate_categories_to_family_scope.sql`) are `SECURITY DEFINER` with `GRANT EXECUTE … TO authenticated` but **no `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC`**, so `anon` retains the default grant. `create_default_hierarchy`'s guard is `IF auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS(...membership...)` — for `anon`, `auth.uid()` is NULL so the guard is **skipped** and it seeds hierarchy rows into any family that has none. 1	# PRD — Family Invitations (invite users to join a family)
2	
3	- **Status:** Draft
4	- **Created:** 2026-07-17
5	- **Surface:** new `family_invitations` table + `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs
6	  (`invite_to_family` / `accept_invite` / `revoke_invite`); a new Family settings
7	  page; the existing email infra (`supabase/functions/_shared/notify.ts`).
8	- **Related:**
9	  - Backlog **"Family editor"** feature (this PRD is its concrete design).
10	  - [Security Remediation PRD](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md) **F1** — the open
11	    `family_members` self-insert policy must be dropped; this feature provides the
12	    _only_ sanctioned membership-write path that replaces it.
13	  - Security **F2** (unverified/non-unique profile emails) — acceptance keys off
14	    the invitee's **verified `auth.users` email**, not profile aliases.
15	  - [domain-model.md](domain-model.md) — Family, Family Member terminology.
16	
17	## Terminology
18	
19	See [domain-model.md](domain-model.md). A **Family** is the data-scoping unit; a
20	**Family Member** is a row in `family_members(family_id, user_id, role, status,
21	is_default)` with `role ∈ {owner, member}` and `status ∈ {active, invited,
22	removed}`. An **Invitation** (new concept) is a pending, email-addressed offer to
23	join a family; it is **not** a membership and grants no access until accepted. UI
24	copy uses "invite" / "family member".
25	
26	## Problem
27	
28	Today a user only ever belongs to the default family created for them at signup by
29	`ensure_default_family()`. There is **no way to add another person to a family** —
30	the "Family editor / invite other users" feature was specced but never built, so
31	households can't actually share an expense view.
32	
33	Naively, the missing piece looks like "let a user insert a `family_members` row."
34	That is exactly the critical **F1** hole: the old `family_members` INSERT policy
35	(`WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid())`) let any authenticated user self-join **any**
36	family. The remediation drops that policy, leaving **no** client membership-write
37	path. This PRD supplies the secure replacement: an invitation flow where every
38	membership write goes through a vetted `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC.
39	
40	## Goals
41	
42	- A family member can invite another person **by email** to their family.
43	- The invitee accepts via a link and becomes an active member — **only** after a
44	  server-side check that the invite is valid and addressed to them.
45	- No path lets a user join a family they weren't invited to (F1 stays closed).
46	- Members can see and **revoke / resend** pending invitations.
47	
48	## Non-goals
49	
50	- **Roles/permissions beyond the existing `owner`/`member`.** No granular
51	  per-category or read-only roles in v1.
52	- **Removing members / leaving a family / transferring ownership** — follow-up
53	  work; this PRD is invite + accept + revoke only.
54	- **Multi-family switching UI.** Users may end up in >1 family via invites; the
55	  default-family selection UX is out of scope (they still operate on their default
56	  family). Flag as an open question.
57	- **In-app notifications / real-time.** Invites are delivered by email only.
58	- Fixing F2 itself. This feature _depends_ on verified auth emails but does not
59	  implement email verification.
60	
61	## Design
62	
63	### D1 — `family_invitations` table (invites are keyed by email, not user_id)
64	
65	An invitee usually has **no account yet**, so there is no `user_id` to store, and
66	we must not create any membership-derived access before acceptance. Therefore
67	invitations live in their own table, addressed by email:
68	
69	| Column          | Notes                                                             |
70	| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
71	| `id`            | uuid pk                                                          |
72	| `family_id`     | → `families(id)` on delete cascade                              |
73	| `invited_email` | normalized `lower(trim(...))`                                    |
74	| `invited_by`    | → `auth.users(id)` (the inviter)                                |
75	| `role`          | `'member'` default (only `owner`/`member` allowed)              |
76	| `token_hash`    | **hash** of a random secret token (store the hash, not the raw) |
77	| `status`        | `pending \| accepted \| revoked \| expired`                     |
78	| `created_at`    | default now()                                                    |
79	| `expires_at`    | default now() + interval (e.g. 7 days)                          |
80	| `accepted_by`   | → `auth.users(id)`, null until accepted                        |
81	| `accepted_at`   | null until accepted                                             |
82	
83	Partial unique index on `(family_id, invited_email) WHERE status = 'pending'` so a
84	family can't accumulate duplicate live invites to the same address.
85	
86	### D2 — Three `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs (the only membership-write path)
87	
88	All three: `SET search_path = public`, `REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC`, `GRANT
89	EXECUTE TO authenticated` (never `anon`). They enforce authorization **inside** the
90	function — never trust the client.
91	
92	1. **`invite_to_family(p_family_id, p_email, p_role)`** — verify the caller is an
93	   **active member** of `p_family_id` (later: require `owner`); reject if the email
94	   already belongs to an active member; insert a `pending` invitation with a fresh
95	   random token + expiry; return the **raw token once** (never stored). The app
96	   then sends the invite email (D4). Enforce a per-family pending-invite cap.
97	2. **`accept_invite(p_token)`** — hash `p_token`, look up a `pending`, non-expired
98	   invitation; **require `auth.users.email` of `auth.uid()` == `invited_email`**
99	   (blocks a forwarded/leaked link being redeemed by someone else); insert
100	   `family_members(family_id, auth.uid(), role, 'active')` `ON CONFLICT DO
101	   NOTHING`; mark the invite `accepted` (`accepted_by`/`accepted_at`). Idempotent.
102	3. **`revoke_invite(p_invitation_id)`** — inviter or an active member of the
103	   family flips `status = 'revoked'`.
104	
105	A scheduled/opportunistic sweep (or a check inside `accept_invite`) treats
106	`expires_at < now()` as `expired`.
107	
108	### D3 — RLS
109	
110	- `family_members`: **no INSERT policy** (F1). SELECT stays the membership-scoped
111	  policy (`is_member_of` helper from the remediation). All inserts flow through the
112	  RPCs, which bypass RLS as definer.
113	- `family_invitations`: SELECT for (a) active members of `family_id` and (b) the
114	  invitee (`invited_email = auth.users.email of auth.uid()`), so a user can see
115	  invites addressed to them. **No** direct client INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy —
116	  mutation only via the RPCs. `token_hash` must never be exposed to the invitee's
117	  SELECT (return a redacted view or omit the column from the client query).
118	
119	### D4 — Email delivery
120	
121	Reuse `supabase/functions/_shared/notify.ts` (Resend). The invite email contains a
122	link `…/invite?token=<raw-token>`. Sender must be `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` on a verified
123	domain (per CLAUDE.md, otherwise Resend 403s). The raw token appears only in the
124	email and the acceptance URL — never persisted server-side.
125	
126	### D5 — UI
127	
128	A **Family** settings page (fulfils the backlog "Family editor"):
129	
130	- Member list (name/email, role, status).
131	- "Invite by email" form → `invite_to_family`.
132	- Pending-invitations list with **Revoke** and **Resend** (resend re-sends the
133	  email; may rotate the token).
134	- A public-ish **`/invite?token=…`** landing page: if signed out, prompt sign-in /
135	  sign-up (carrying the token through auth), then call `accept_invite`; show
136	  success / expired / wrong-account states.
137	
138	### D6 — Token security
139	
140	- Random ≥ 32 bytes; store only a hash (`token_hash`); compare by hashing the
141	  presented token. A DB read then can't yield a usable link.
142	- Single-use (status → `accepted`) and time-boxed (`expires_at`).

lines: - **✅ DONE — family_members self-join closed.** The open `"Users can insert their own membership"` INSERT policy (which, with the `USING(true)` SELECT, let any authed user self-join any family for a whole-tenant breach) was **dropped** in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql`. There is now no client membership-write path — legitimate membership goes through the `SECURITY DEFINER` `ensure_default_family()` (bypasses RLS). Verified live 2026-07-17 (self-insert into an arbitrary family rejected). The sanctioned invite-based replacement is designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md).

- **🟠 HIGH SECURITY — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint** (`002_profiles_table.sql`). The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix (abuse is by a legit authed user). Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.

- **✅ DONE — anon-executable seed functions locked down.** `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` carried a **direct** `anon` EXECUTE grant (Supabase default privileges), so `anon` could seed rows into empty tenants. `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` revoked `FROM PUBLIC`, but live testing showed that missed the direct anon grant (the call still executed, blocked only by a FK) — so `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql` added explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`; `authenticated` keeps its grant (the `CategoryService` caller). Verified live 2026-07-17. **Lesson learned:** on Supabase, `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` alone does NOT remove `anon`/`authenticated` — they hold *direct* grants via default privileges, so revoke those roles explicitly. (Still open: a sweep of any *other* `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for the same missing REVOKE.)

-- **🟢 LOW SECURITY / deferred audit items still open (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Still present, unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` unauthenticated + SSRF via caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, incl. svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`) — the secret-prefix leak was fixed in the refactor but these two survived; **M2** `/admin/resize-images` is a client-only page that deletes+re-uploads receipt originals with no authz beyond `confirm()`; **M3** `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding / no limit). Also **F6:** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject (`20260705_email_send_failures.sql`) — confirm intended. Note **`receipts` UPDATE `WITH CHECK`** carries the same `fm.family_id = fm.family_id` tautology as INSERT — already in scope of the PRD's **R3** (which lists both `:347` INSERT and `:370` UPDATE).

Also **F6:** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject (`20260705_email_send_failures.sql`) — confirm intended. Note **`receipts` UPDATE `WITH CHECK`** carries the same `fm.family_id = fm.family_id` tautology as INSERT — already in scope of the PRD's **R3** (which lists both `:347` INSERT and `:370` UPDATE).

- **Remove the abandoned Spending Bridge (waterfall) view. ✅ DONE.** Built as a 3rd `/spending` view then abandoned as not intuitive — [ADR-0004](adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) (reminder screenshot `docs/BridgeChartTooWide.png`). Deleted `SpendingBridge.svelte`, `spendingWaterfall.ts`, and their `.spec.ts`; stripped the `Bridge` toggle, render branch, `'bridge'` view type, and `priorReport` state from `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte`. Full suite green (1424), `check`/eslint/Prettier clean. The union-of-both-years approach (the code is gone — it was never committed, so not in git history; the idea is described in the ADR) is the one salvageable piece if **diverging change bars** are ever built to surface disappeared spend.

- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), CVE-2023-30533, fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), CVE-2024-22363, fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist but **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there's no fix version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, fully contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` (`convertExcelToCSV`/`isExcelFile`, ~4 API calls) behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx` (tests build both, `ExcelToCSVConverter.test.ts`). Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball (`xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/...` via `overrides`) — clears the CVEs, keeps `.xls` support, but adds a non-npm-registry dep that our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — actively maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`** (xlsx/csv only), so it would drop `.xls` support unless paired with a dedicated BIFF parser (`js-xls`). Decision needed on whether legacy `.xls` is still required. Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers the practical risk.

- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie` rather than force it. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix` (non-breaking). Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.
